modified_caption: (a) Training loss trajectories across iterations for various model configurations. The line plot depicts the change in loss over training iterations, with the x-axis labeled "#Iteration" (0 to 140,000) and the y-axis labeled "Loss" (2.4 to 3.4). Six model configurations are compared: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). The Vanilla model (purple) exhibits the highest initial loss, declining sharply to approximately 2.7 by 10,000 iterations and gradually stabilizing near 2.45. StrmLLM (n=64) (blue) demonstrates a more rapid initial decline, reaching 2.6 by 20,000 iterations, but ultimately plateaus at roughly 2.75, consistently exceeding the loss of all other configurations beyond 40,000 iterations. SepLLM (n=64) (orange) and SepLLM (n=64, H) (green) follow nearly identical trajectories, with losses converging around 2.52 and 2.51, respectively, though SepLLM (n=64) initially declines at a marginally slower rate. SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red) stabilizes prematurely, maintaining a loss of approximately 2.65 after 60,000 iterations, indicating diminished optimization efficiency. SepLLM (n=128) (blue-violet) achieves the lowest final loss, descending to 2.48, and exhibits the most consistent downward trend, with minimal fluctuations. A vertical green line at iteration 0 demarcates the onset of training. The legend is positioned in the top-right corner.

modifications.claim: StrmLLM (n=64) (blue) ultimately plateaus at roughly 2.75, consistently exceeding the loss of all other configurations beyond 40,000 iterations.
modifications.reality: StrmLLM (n=64) (blue) actually plateaus near 2.6, not 2.75, and does not consistently exceed the loss of all other configurations; it remains above SepLLM variants but below Vanilla after 40,000 iterations.

modifications.claim: SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red) stabilizes prematurely, maintaining a loss of approximately 2.65 after 60,000 iterations, indicating diminished optimization efficiency.
modifications.reality: SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red) does not stabilize at 2.65; it continues to decline and ends near 2.49, with no evidence of premature stabilization or diminished efficiency.

modifications.claim: SepLLM (n=64) (orange) initially declines at a marginally slower rate than SepLLM (n=64, H) (green).
modifications.reality: SepLLM (n=64) (orange) and SepLLM (n=64, H) (green) decline at nearly identical rates initially, with no discernible difference in the rate of loss reduction.
